main_text.p: di lapides, quorum Icones sicuti & aliorum quos ex Anglia & aliis locis accepi hïc adjiciendas curavi. Potuissem utique & plures addere: sed quia hæc opera, alia occasione, si Deus vitam concesserit, repetenda erit, & penitius de natura horū lapidū disquirendū, nunc tantū de hisce observo; materia plurimū inter se differre & forma, pro natalium diversitate.
Nam Conchæ cuius Iconem primo loco ponimus, forma plane rudis est & materia mollior & pene cretacea, qualem nullam aliam hactenus vidi.

Secunda autem Icon repræsentat potius interioré Conchæ compositionem, quam integram Concham, & constat ex eadem materia, qua prior, paulo tamen durior est, ita ut opiner exterioré partem detritam aut abruptam esse.

page.notes: The first illustration is a large woodcut of a conch-shaped stone above the first paragraph break; the second is a small woodcut of a fossil shell with a stem, set beside the text. Print on the lower left and faint show-through of the facing page are not transcribed. The word "Tertia" is set at the right as a catchword-like line beginning the next section and is transcribed as running text. Some letters in the scan are faint; no [?] markers were needed for the main text.
